title: Barcelona vs. Real Madrid Combined XI: Red-Hot La Liga Leaders Dominate
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath3:00 PM EDTThe biggest club game in the world features some of the game’s great stars.  / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesCircled in thick red marker pen since the fixture list was announced, the first Clásico of the season is upon us with Barcelona hosting Real Madrid at Camp Nou on Sunday.
The meeting of Spain’s great rivals is always box office, but the match has reached new levels of anticipation this autumn, amid a sea of narratives.
José Mourinho returns to the fixture for the first time in 13 years, bringing all the bad blood, baggage and conspiracy theories that contribute to the creation of absolute cinema.

Amid the melodrama, Barcelona’s lightning start means Madrid really need to come out fighting in this game or face the uncomfortable reality that La Liga might be out of their grasp before Mariah Carey has even hit the airwaves.
With a who’s who of the game’s great and good on show, here’s a combined XI of the two rivals’ available players.

Thibaut Courtois is Madrid’s Mr. Dependable. / Alcoba Beitia/Getty ImagesIn reality, there is very little to choose from between two of the best keepers in the business. Joan García was handed both La Liga’s Zamora Trophy (for the league’s best goalkeeper) and the Save of the Season award in 2025–26 and has proven a remarkable signing for Barcelona since joining from Espanyol in 2025.

Courtois though, on his day, is arguably still the best keeper in the world. The 34-year-old has kept only two clean sheets all season, but can hardly be blamed for Madrid’s leakiness. The Belgian has made 29 saves so far in 2026–27 to García’s 15, and boasts a superior save percentage at 76.3% to 68.2%.

Xavi Espart is enjoying a breakthrough season. / Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press Sports/Europa Press/Getty ImagesWith José Mourinho cycling unconvincingly between Denzel Dumfries, Trent Alexander-Arnold and Federico Valverde, the Barça option is the obvious choice.

A barely known quantity prior to this season, Espart—another gem from Barça’s fabled class of 2007—has shone on both sides of the defense this season, despite coming through the academy system as a midfielder.

An emergency option midweek, the 19-year-old shut down both Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Désiré Doué against PSG—he wasn’t dribbled past once all game—and popped up with a goal, showcasing his fine attacking instincts.

Pau Cubarsí is the favorite for the Golden Boy award. / BSR Agency/Getty ImagesNamed the Young Player of the Tournament at the 2026 World Cup, Cubarsí is the favorite to win the coveted Golden Boy award after a sensational year for Barcelona and Spain.

The 19-year-old played every minute of Spain’s triumph in North America and is now well-established as Barça’s key center back. No player in La Liga averages more passes per game this season than Cubarsí’s 98.8.

Dean Huijsen has earned José Mourinho’s trust. /  Ion Alcoba Beitia/Getty ImagesAfter a middling debut season last summer, Huijsen has looked more assured as the ball player at the heart of Los Blancos’ defense so far in 2026–27—Madrid derby red card aside.
The Dutch-born Spain international is regularly the player on the pitch with the most touches, passes and defensive contributions.

Marc Cucurella’s signing was seen as a coup for Madrid. /  Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid/Getty ImagesMuch was expected of Cucurella when he joined Real Madrid from Chelsea at the outset of the summer. However, the Bernabéu is still yet to see the very best of the World Cup winner.

During the last international break, Luis de la Fuente admitted Cucurella was among those stars who raise their game when pulling on a Spain jersey, saying: “With us, something happens... When they join the national team, they transform. Some sometimes show a level far superior to what they show at their club.”
Still, on his day Cucurella remains a tenacious pest of a defender; a two-way threat as capable of contributing to his team’s attacks as he is at snuffing out those of the opposition.

Rodri could’ve joined Madrid this summer. / Joan Valls/Urbanandsport/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesCoveted by both Clásico clubs in the summer, Barcelona were the pick of the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner—and they are all the better for it.
There is simply no more complete midfielder in the game than Rodri—a one-man shield, conductor and metronome.
